title: What adverts do to persuade us
titleChinese: 广告中说服消费者购物的策略
paragraphs: Adverts are designed to persuade us, but which techniques have been shown to be effective in enticing us to buy things?

One way is simply to portray something as normal. Former advertising professional Dan Parker explains that 'normalisation', showing people happily eating unhealthily, can lead to higher sales of junk food as people start to see these habits as normal. This is like product placement, where products are shown or mentioned in TV shows and films. Beth Fossen, an assistant professor of marketing, tells us that product placement is most effective when it is not too obvious. We become defensive if we know that someone is trying to sell us something. It seems that a subtle approach can be more convincing.

Appealing to our emotions is another strategy that advertisers use. Some of them use fear to persuade us. Jannet Pendleton, a senior lecturer in communication studies, explains that for fear to be an effective tool, we need to believe that both the fears raised, and the possibility that our actions can make a difference are credible. Where fears are exaggerated or we feel helpless, we are likely to switch off. Adverts often show perfect-looking people because marketers believe that we will aspire to be like them and buy the products they endorse. However, as Karen Middleton, a senior lecturer in marketing and advertising, points out, this may not be the best strategy. The research that she mentions shows these adverts can make people feel bad and put them off products. These studies say that seeing a more human and relatable side of people can sway us into believing them. David Robson, writing for BBC Worklife, explains that endorsements from characters who admit their mistakes can often be more believable.

So, it seems that the secret to these persuasion techniques is that, to be most effective, they need to be used carefully. Perhaps the best technique advertisers can use to persuade people is to fully understand the people they are selling to.

vocabulary.entry: advert /ˈædvɜːt/ n. 广告 【口语词汇】
vocabulary.example: I saw your advert in the local paper.
vocabulary.translation: 我在当地报纸上看到了你们的广告。

vocabulary.entry: entice /ɪnˈtaɪs/ v. 引诱；吸引；诱惑
vocabulary.example: The bargain prices are expected to entice customers away from other stores.
vocabulary.translation: 低廉的价格预计会把顾客从其他商店吸引过来。

vocabulary.entry: portray /pɔːˈtreɪ/ v. 描绘；刻画；将…描绘成 【书面词汇】
vocabulary.example: The painting portrays a beautiful young woman in a blue dress.
vocabulary.translation: 这幅画描绘了一位身穿蓝色连衣裙的美丽年轻女子。

vocabulary.entry: normalisation /ˌnɔːməlaɪˈzeɪʃn/ n. 常态化；正常化 【书面词汇】
vocabulary.example: The two sides signed a treaty aimed at the normalisation of diplomatic relations.
vocabulary.translation: 双方签署了一项旨在实现外交关系正常化的条约。

vocabulary.entry: unhealthily /ʌnˈhelθɪli/ adv. 不健康地
vocabulary.example: Many young people eat unhealthily and don't get enough exercise.
vocabulary.translation: 很多年轻人饮食不健康，也缺乏足够的锻炼。

vocabulary.entry: junk food /dʒʌŋk fuːd/ n. 垃圾食品
vocabulary.example: My doctor told me to cut down on junk food and eat more vegetables.
vocabulary.translation: 医生让我少吃垃圾食品，多吃蔬菜。

vocabulary.entry: product placement /ˈprɒdʌkt ˈpleɪsmənt/ n. 植入式广告
vocabulary.example: The film includes a lot of product placement for soft drinks and cars.
vocabulary.translation: 这部电影里有大量软饮和汽车的植入式广告。

vocabulary.entry: marketing /ˈmɑːkɪtɪŋ/ n. 市场营销；营销
vocabulary.example: The product's success is due to its clever marketing.
vocabulary.translation: 这款产品的成功归功于其巧妙的营销。

vocabulary.entry: defensive /dɪˈfensɪv/ adj. 戒备的；有戒心的；防御性的
vocabulary.example: He always gets defensive if you mention his past mistakes.
vocabulary.translation: 如果你提起他过去的错误，他总是会变得很有戒心。

vocabulary.entry: subtle /ˈsʌtl/ adj. 含蓄的；不易察觉的；微妙的 【书面词汇】
vocabulary.example: There's a subtle difference in meaning between the two words.
vocabulary.translation: 这两个词在词义上有细微的差别。

vocabulary.entry: convincing /kənˈvɪnsɪŋ/ adj. 有说服力的；令人信服的
vocabulary.example: She gave a very convincing argument against the proposal.
vocabulary.translation: 她提出了非常有说服力的论据来反对这项提案。

vocabulary.entry: appeal to /əˈpiːl tuː/ 短语 诉诸；迎合；对…有吸引力
vocabulary.example: The new policy is designed to appeal to young voters.
vocabulary.translation: 这项新政策旨在迎合年轻选民。

vocabulary.entry: strategy /ˈstrætədʒi/ n. 策略；战略；规划 【书面词汇】
vocabulary.example: The company has developed a new marketing strategy to boost sales.
vocabulary.translation: 该公司制定了新的营销策略来提升销量。

vocabulary.entry: advertiser /ˈædvətaɪzə(r)/ n. 广告商；广告客户
vocabulary.example: Advertisers are always looking for new ways to reach potential customers.
vocabulary.translation: 广告商一直在寻找触达潜在客户的新方式。

vocabulary.entry: lecturer /ˈlektʃərə(r)/ n. 讲师；演讲者 【书面词汇】
vocabulary.example: She's a senior lecturer in economics at the University of Leeds.
vocabulary.translation: 她是利兹大学经济学专业的高级讲师。

vocabulary.entry: credible /ˈkredəbl/ adj. 可信的；可靠的；有可信度的 【书面词汇】
vocabulary.example: The witness gave a credible account of what happened that night.
vocabulary.translation: 证人对当晚发生的事情给出了可信的陈述。

vocabulary.entry: exaggerated /ɪɡˈzædʒəreɪtɪd/ adj. 夸大的；夸张的；言过其实的
vocabulary.example: The newspaper gave an exaggerated account of the incident.
vocabulary.translation: 报纸对这一事件的报道言过其实。

vocabulary.entry: helpless /ˈhelpləs/ adj. 无助的；无能为力的
vocabulary.example: He felt helpless in the face of the company's decision to close the factory.
vocabulary.translation: 面对公司关闭工厂的决定，他感到无能为力。

vocabulary.entry: switch off /swɪtʃ ɒf/ 短语 失去兴趣；产生抵触 【口语词汇】
vocabulary.example: I switch off when he starts talking about cars all the time.
vocabulary.translation: 他一没完没了说起汽车，我就没兴趣听了。

vocabulary.entry: marketer /ˈmɑːkɪtə(r)/ n. 营销人员；营销商
vocabulary.example: Marketers need to understand the needs of their target audience.
vocabulary.translation: 营销人员需要了解目标受众的需求。

vocabulary.entry: aspire /əˈspaɪə(r)/ v. 渴望；立志；追求 【书面词汇】
vocabulary.example: Many young people aspire to become famous actors and singers.
vocabulary.translation: 很多年轻人都立志成为知名的演员和歌手。

vocabulary.entry: endorse /ɪnˈdɔːs/ v. 代言；背书；认可；支持 【书面词汇】
vocabulary.example: The celebrity earns millions endorsing luxury brands.
vocabulary.translation: 这位名人靠代言奢侈品牌赚了数百万。

vocabulary.entry: put off /pʊt ɒf/ 短语 使反感；使失去兴趣；使却步
vocabulary.example: The high prices put many customers off buying the new phone.
vocabulary.translation: 高昂的价格让很多顾客打消了买这款新手机的念头。

vocabulary.entry: relatable /rɪˈleɪtəbl/ adj. 能产生共鸣的；接地气的
vocabulary.example: The main character in the novel is very relatable to young readers.
vocabulary.translation: 小说的主角能让年轻读者产生强烈的共鸣。

vocabulary.entry: sway /sweɪ/ v. 影响；使改变看法；说服 【书面词汇】
vocabulary.example: Nothing you say will sway her decision to move abroad.
vocabulary.translation: 无论你说什么，都改变不了她移居国外的决定。

vocabulary.entry: endorsement /ɪnˈdɔːsmənt/ n. 代言；背书；认可 【书面词汇】
vocabulary.example: The company's new campaign features endorsements from several top athletes.
vocabulary.translation: 该公司的新宣传活动请到了多位顶级运动员代言。

vocabulary.entry: believable /bɪˈliːvəbl/ adj. 可信的；令人信服的
vocabulary.example: The plot of the movie is not very believable.
vocabulary.translation: 这部电影的剧情不太可信。

vocabulary.entry: persuasion /pəˈsweɪʒn/ n. 说服；劝说；说服力 【书面词汇】
vocabulary.example: It took a lot of persuasion to get her to agree to the plan.
vocabulary.translation: 费了很大的口舌才说服她同意这个计划。

sentences.english: Adverts are designed to persuade us, but which techniques have been shown to be effective in enticing us to buy things?
sentences.chinese: 广告旨在说服我们购买商品，但哪些技巧已被证实是有效的哪？

sentences.english: One way is simply to portray something as normal.
sentences.chinese: 一种方法就是将某事物描绘成常态。

sentences.english: Former advertising professional Dan Parker explains that 'normalisation', showing people happily eating unhealthily, can lead to higher sales of junk food as people start to see these habits as normal.
sentences.chinese: 前广告从业者丹·帕克解释说，“常态化”——展现人们开心地吃不健康食品——会使垃圾食品销量攀升，因为人们会开始将这些习惯视为正常。

sentences.english: This is like product placement, where products are shown or mentioned in TV shows and films.
sentences.chinese: 这类似于植入式广告，即在影视剧里展示或提及产品。

sentences.english: Beth Fossen, an assistant professor of marketing, tells us that product placement is most effective when it is not too obvious.
sentences.chinese: 市场营销助理教授贝丝·福森告诉我们，植入式广告在不那么显眼时效果最佳。

sentences.english: We become defensive if we know that someone is trying to sell us something.
sentences.chinese: 如果我们知道有人试图向我们推销东西，就会产生戒备心。

sentences.english: It seems that a subtle approach can be more convincing.
sentences.chinese: 似乎隐晦的方式更具说服力。

sentences.english: Appealing to our emotions is another strategy that advertisers use.
sentences.chinese: 诉诸情感是广告商使用的另一种策略。

sentences.english: Some of them use fear to persuade us.
sentences.chinese: 部分广告商会利用恐惧来说服我们。

sentences.english: Jannet Pendleton, a senior lecturer in communication studies, explains that for fear to be an effective tool, we need to believe that both the fears raised, and the possibility that our actions can make a difference are credible.
sentences.chinese: 传播学高级讲师詹妮特·彭德尔顿解释说，要让恐惧成为有效工具，我们必须相信所引起的恐惧以及自身行动能带来改变的可能性都是可信的。

sentences.english: Where fears are exaggerated or we feel helpless, we are likely to switch off.
sentences.chinese: 如果恐惧被夸大，或是我们感到无助，就很可能会抵触。

sentences.english: Adverts often show perfect-looking people because marketers believe that we will aspire to be like them and buy the products they endorse.
sentences.chinese: 广告常展示形象完美的人，因为营销人员认为我们会渴望成为那样的人，并购买他们代言的产品。

sentences.english: However, as Karen Middleton, a senior lecturer in marketing and advertising, points out, this may not be the best strategy.
sentences.chinese: 然而，市场营销与广告学高级讲师卡伦·米德尔顿指出，这或许并非最佳策略。

sentences.english: The research that she mentions shows these adverts can make people feel bad and put them off products.
sentences.chinese: 她提及的研究表明，这类广告会让人产生负面情绪，进而对产品产生反感。

sentences.english: These studies say that seeing a more human and relatable side of people can sway us into believing them.
sentences.chinese: 这些研究称，看到人们更真实、更易共情的一面，会让我们更愿意相信他们。

sentences.english: David Robson, writing for BBC Worklife, explains that endorsements from characters who admit their mistakes can often be more believable.
sentences.chinese: 为BBC职场专栏撰稿的戴维·罗布森解释道，承认自身错误的人物所做的代言往往更可信。

sentences.english: So, it seems that the secret to these persuasion techniques is that, to be most effective, they need to be used carefully.
sentences.chinese: 由此看来，这些说服技巧的关键在于，要想效果最佳，就必须谨慎运用。

sentences.english: Perhaps the best technique advertisers can use to persuade people is to fully understand the people they are selling to.
sentences.chinese: 或许广告商能用来说服人们的最佳技巧，就是充分了解目标受众。
